newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil steady at high level.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil steady at high level.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Tuesday at a higher level on fresh prompt buying support despite a weaker crude, traders said.
"Fuel oil is steady this afternoon after this morning's big increase but the market is very quiet," one broker said.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $101.75/$102.50 per tonne, up from Monday's $101/$102, brokers said.
The strength of the front month was not carried on to the forward months with July quoted at $99.50/$100.25, from $100/101 on Monday.
Traders said the widening spread was partly due to a lack of market confidence in the further out months as many feel that the current physical buying support will not be extended to July.
In the physical market, a local trader had over the past week bought about three 20,000-tonne cargoes with the latest traded at $103.50 per tonne on Monday.
The purchases coincided with a reduction in exports from the Middle East due to the strong domestic demand there for the summer which has led to firmer prices.
Prices are poised to gain further strength over the next few days if the buying continues unabated as supplies are limited and sellers might wait for the bids to increase before selling, they said.
Gas oil edged up by 10 cents late afternoon from the morning in quiet trade with June swaps last quoted at $25.45/$25.55 per barrel, but down 10 cents from Thursday.
Traders said the firmer prices were in anticipation of fresh buying support in the physical market.
"The bids were at a low level on Monday and some people expect the buyers to raise their prices later today," one trader said.
Bids were seen on Monday at $25.40 per barrel, down 30 cents from Friday's traded level despite the firmer crude market over the weekend.
